experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the medieval cobblestone streets of Staré Město, witness the iconic Orloj Astronomical Clock chime on the hour, and explore the Gothic Týn Church. Join a free walking tour to uncover centuries of Bohemian history, Jewish Quarter secrets, and stunning Baroque architecture without breaking the budget.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl & Local Street Food Night
experiences.description: Dive into Budapest's legendary ruin bar scene starting at Szimpla Kert in the Jewish Quarter. Graze on local street food including lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese), kürtőskalács (chimney cake), and paprika-spiced sausages from nearby market stalls. A quintessential Budapest evening blending bohemian culture with authentic Hungarian flavors.

experiences.name: Thermal Bathing at Széchenyi Baths
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most magnificent thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. Enjoy indoor and outdoor geothermal pools at a constant 38°C, steam rooms, and saunas. A deeply local experience that Budapestians have cherished for over a century — the perfect cultural and wellness activity mid-trip.

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex & Golden Lane Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a half-day exploring the world's largest ancient castle complex, perched dramatically above the Vltava River. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral, the Royal Palace, and the charming Golden Lane — a row of tiny colorful medieval houses once inhabited by castle guards and alchemists. The panoramic views over Prague's red-roofed skyline are absolutely breathtaking.

experiences.name: Budapest Great Market Hall Food & Culture Immersion
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent 19th-century Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok), a cathedral of Hungarian gastronomy. Sample house-made salami, aged Mangalica pork products, pickled vegetables, and paprika varieties from local vendors. Pick up handcrafted folk embroidery and Herend porcelain souvenirs on the upper floor. A feast for all the senses that captures the soul of Hungarian culture and cuisine.
experiences.location: Central Market Hall, District IX, Budapest

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A — Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A — In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Prague Václav Havel Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Airport Express bus (Line AE) or night bus 910 to the city center. Check in to your accommodation, grab a late-night snack from a 24-hour convenience store or nearby kebab stand near Wenceslas Square. Rest and prepare for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night street food — try a trdelník (chimney cake) or a quick kebab from a stand near Wenceslas Square for under €5

day_by_day.notes: Keep it simple on arrival night. Buy a Prague public transport pass at the airport (24-hour or 3-day pass is very cost-effective). Exchange a small amount of currency to Czech Koruna (CZK) at the airport — avoid airport exchange booths with poor rates; use an ATM instead.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a leisurely breakfast, then head to Prague Old Town (Staré Město). Walk across the iconic Charles Bridge (free) in the morning before the crowds arrive. Admire the baroque statues and views of Prague Castle. Explore the Old Town Square and watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour — free to watch from outside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb the Old Town Hall Tower (small fee ~€6) for panoramic views of the city. Wander through the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — the exterior and streets are free to explore, though synagogue interiors require a paid ticket (~€15 if interested). Head to Náměstí Míru area for a quieter local vibe and window-shop the local markets.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across Charles Bridge at sunset for stunning golden-hour views. Head to the Vinohrady neighborhood for dinner at a local Czech pub (hospoda). Try svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings. End the night with a cheap local Czech beer — Prague is famous for having some of the cheapest quality beer in Europe.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry and coffee at a local bakery near your accommodation — budget ~€3-4
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá or similar traditional Czech pub lunch — daily lunch specials (polední menu) cost ~€5-7 including soup and main course
meals.dinner: U Sudu or a local hospoda in Vinohrady — hearty Czech meal with beer for ~€8-10

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Old Town is very walkable. Avoid tourist trap restaurants directly on Old Town Square as prices are 2-3x higher. Look for 'polední menu' (lunch menu) boards outside restaurants for the best value meals.

day_by_day.morning: Take tram or walk up to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Purchase the short circuit ticket (~€10) to visit St. Vitus Cathedral, Old Royal Palace, and St. George's Basilica. The castle grounds and outer courtyards are free to roam. Enjoy sweeping views over Prague's red-roofed cityscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down through the charming Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood. Explore the narrow cobblestone streets, baroque gardens, and colorful buildings. Visit Kampa Island and the quirky John Lennon Wall (free). Cross back over Charles Bridge and explore Nové Město (New Town) including Wenceslas Square — a center of Czech history and modern life.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free walking tour of Prague (tip-based, budget €5-10 tip for the guide) — many depart from Old Town Square in the evenings and cover hidden gems and local legends. Afterward, grab dinner in the Žižkov district — a bohemian, non-touristy neighborhood with cheap local eateries and bars.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre-style budget alternative — try Café Nona or a local café for toast, eggs, and coffee ~€4-5
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from Manifesto Market or a local supermarket (Albert or Billa) near Malá Strana — bread, cheese, cold cuts, and local snacks for ~€4
meals.dinner: Žižkov local pub dinner — try fried cheese (smažený sýr) with tartar sauce, a classic Czech budget dish, with beer ~€7-9

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is best visited early morning to avoid crowds. The free walking tours are excellent value — search for 'Prague Free Tours' or 'Sandeman's New Prague Tours' online. Žižkov is slightly off the tourist trail but very authentic and affordable.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods on foot — admire the art nouveau and cubist architecture. Visit the National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square (~€8 entry) — a grand neo-renaissance building with natural history and Czech history exhibits. Alternatively, the Museum of Communism (~€12) offers a fascinating look at life behind the Iron Curtain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Vyšehrad Fortress (free entry to grounds) — a peaceful hilltop fortress with stunning views of the Vltava River, a historic cemetery with famous Czech graves, and far fewer tourists than Prague Castle. Pack a snack and enjoy the gardens. Head back to the city center and browse the Havelské tržiště (Havel's Market) for affordable souvenirs and fresh produce.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your last evening in Prague. Take a budget Vltava River walk along the embankment at dusk. Have dinner at a classic Czech restaurant in Nové Město. Pack your bags tonight as tomorrow you depart for Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh obložený chlebíček (open-faced sandwich) from a local deli or potraviny (corner store) ~€2-3
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Vietnamese restaurant — Prague has a large Vietnamese community with excellent, ultra-cheap pho and banh mi for ~€4-6 (try Pho Vietnam Tuan & Lan)
meals.dinner: Farewell Czech dinner — try Restaurace U Parlamentu or similar for svíčková or roast duck with red cabbage ~€10-12 including beer

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is a hidden gem and far less crowded than other Prague sights — perfect for a relaxed afternoon. Stock up on Czech beer or Becherovka liqueur as affordable souvenirs from a supermarket before leaving. Check bus/train schedules to Budapest tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Prague to Budapest. The most budget-friendly option is the FlixBus or RegioJet bus (~€15-25, approximately 7-8 hours) or a train via Bratislava (~€20-35, 6-7 hours). Book in advance for the cheapest fares. Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside en route. Pack snacks and a reusable water bottle for the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest in the afternoon. Check in to your accommodation. Take a brief orientation walk around your neighborhood. Budapest is divided by the Danube into Buda (hilly, historic) and Pest (flat, vibrant) — get your bearings. Head to the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) before it closes (~5pm on Saturdays) to browse fresh produce, Hungarian paprika, salami, and affordable street food on the upper floor.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Danube Promenade on the Pest side for your first iconic view of the illuminated Buda Castle and Chain Bridge at night — completely free and breathtaking. Grab dinner in the lively 7th District (the Jewish Quarter / ruin bar district). Explore Gozsdu Udvar, a series of interconnected courtyards filled with bars and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks from a Prague supermarket the night before for the journey — bread, fruit, yogurt ~€3
meals.lunch: Bus/train station food or packed lunch on board — budget €4-6
meals.dinner: Lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor at the Great Market Hall or nearby for ~€3, plus a sit-down meal at a ruin bar in the 7th District for ~€8-10

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague-Budapest transport at least a few days in advance for the best budget prices. RegioJet offers comfortable buses with free Wi-Fi and onboard entertainment. Upon arrival in Budapest, buy a Budapest public transport pass (24-hour ~€3 or 72-hour ~€8) — the metro, trams, and buses are excellent.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot to the Buda side. Hike or take the funicular (~€3 one way) up Castle Hill. Explore Buda Castle District — visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom, ~€5 entry) and the Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — the exterior terraces offer some of the most iconic panoramic views of Budapest and the Danube for free (inner towers have a small fee).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down from Castle Hill through the charming streets of Víziváros (Watertown). Cross back to Pest via the Chain Bridge. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — exterior is free and stunning; guided tours available (~€8 for EU citizens, €16 for non-EU). Walk along the Danube and spot the haunting 'Shoes on the Danube Bank' Holocaust memorial (free).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe, beautiful even from the outside (entry ~€12 if interested). Explore the 7th District's famous ruin bars — start with Szimpla Kert, the original and most iconic ruin bar. Enjoy cheap local draft beer (Dreher or Borsodi) for ~€1.50-2 per pint.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local pékség (bakery) — fresh kifli rolls, pogácsa (savory scones), and coffee for ~€3
meals.lunch: Goulash soup (gulyásleves) at a local étterem (restaurant) in the Castle District — look for daily lunch menus for ~€6-8
meals.dinner: Street food evening in the 7th District — kürtőskalács (chimney cake), lángos, or a quick falafel from a local spot for ~€4-6, with cheap ruin bar drinks

day_by_day.notes: Sunday morning at Fisherman's Bastion is magical — arrive early before tour groups. The ruin bars of Budapest are a unique cultural experience — they are built in abandoned buildings and courtyards and are quintessentially Budapest. Szimpla Kert also hosts a Sunday farmers market in the mornings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Széchenyi Thermal Baths (Széchenyi gyógyfürdő) — one of Budapest's most iconic experiences. Morning entry on weekdays is cheaper (~€18-22 for cabin entry). Soak in the outdoor and indoor thermal pools set in a stunning neo-baroque building in City Park. This is a quintessential Budapest cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) — stroll through the park, see Vajdahunyad Castle (exterior free), and visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere), a grand UNESCO-listed monument commemorating Hungarian history — completely free. Walk down Andrássy Avenue, Budapest's grand boulevard lined with neo-renaissance mansions, toward the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the New York Café for a coffee — it's a splurge (~€5-7 for a coffee) but the interior is one of the most ornate cafés in the world and worth a quick visit. Head to the Pest riverside for the evening light show on the Parliament building. Dinner in the 5th or 6th District at a traditional Hungarian étterem.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the baths — yogurt and fruit from a local market or supermarket ~€3
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or grab food from a local büfé (snack bar) near City Park — Hungarian sausage sandwich (virsli) or a slice of pizza ~€3-5
meals.dinner: Traditional Hungarian dinner — try chicken paprikash (paprikás csirke) with nokedli (egg noodles) at a local étterem in the 6th District ~€9-12

day_by_day.notes: Book Széchenyi Baths online in advance to save time and sometimes get a small discount. Bring flip flops, a towel, and a padlock for the locker. A swimsuit is required. The baths are a genuine local wellness institution, not just a tourist attraction — locals use them regularly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Central Market Hall (same as Great Market Hall) for last-minute souvenir shopping: Hungarian paprika, Pick salami, Tokaji wine, and palinka (fruit brandy) are all excellent and affordable gifts. Browse the upper floor food stalls for a hearty Hungarian breakfast. Walk along the Váci utca (pedestrian shopping street) one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum, ~€4) for a final dose of Central European history, covering Hungarian history from prehistoric times to the present. Alternatively, explore the Liberty Bridge (Szabadság híd) area and climb Gellért Hill (free) for a final panoramic farewell view of Budapest — the view from the Citadella is one of the best in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final budget farewell dinner in Budapest before heading to the airport or your onward destination. Reflect on the incredible history, culture, and food of Prague and Budapest. Head to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport via the 100E airport bus (~€3) or Minibud shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Hearty Hungarian breakfast at the Great Market Hall upper floor — lángos or stuffed pancakes (palacsinta) ~€4-5
meals.lunch: Final Hungarian lunch — try halászlé (spicy fisherman's soup) or a classic pörkölt (meat stew) at a local restaurant near the museum ~€7-9
meals.dinner: Light farewell meal — grab a chimney cake, some kürtős, or a quick meal at a local étterem near the airport transport hub ~€6-8

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for airport travel and check-in from central Budapest. The 100E airport bus is the cheapest option to the airport. Use any remaining Hungarian Forints (HUF) at the airport or exchange back — coins cannot be exchanged so spend them. Overall trip budget estimate: €400-600 per person including transport, accommodation, food, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: N/A — Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A — In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Prague Václav Havel Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Airport Express bus or a pre-booked taxi to your accommodation. Check in, freshen up, and take a short relaxing stroll around the immediate neighborhood if energy allows.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night bite near the hotel — look for a local 24-hour bistro or a convenience deli for light snacks such as chlebíčky (Czech open-faced sandwiches) and a cold Pilsner Urquell

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 extremely light. Pre-book airport transfer in advance to avoid stress upon late arrival. Confirm hotel late check-in policy before travel.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then head to Prague Old Town (Staré Město). Explore the iconic Old Town Square, admire the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and watch the hourly chime show, and wander through the medieval lanes. Visit the Church of Our Lady before Týn for a glimpse of Gothic architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross Charles Bridge on foot, soaking in panoramic views of the Vltava River and Prague Castle. Climb up to Prague Castle Complex — explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Enjoy sweeping views over the red-roofed city from the castle ramparts.
day_by_day.evening: Descend from the castle into Malá Strana (Lesser Town). Stroll through charming cobblestone streets and settle into a cozy local restaurant for a traditional Czech dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café — try a fresh pastry and coffee at Café Louvre or a local bakery
meals.lunch: Casual lunch near Charles Bridge — Lokál Malá Strana offers authentic Czech cuisine at mid-range prices; try svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) with bread dumplings
meals.dinner: Dinner at U Modré Kachničky (The Blue Duckling) in Malá Strana — known for classic Bohemian dishes like roast duck with red cabbage; mid-range pricing

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Prague's cobblestones can be tough on feet. The castle area gets busy mid-morning; aim to arrive by 10:00 AM. Prague Card can save money on multiple attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of the best-preserved Jewish historic districts in Europe. Tour the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Pinkas Synagogue (Holocaust memorial), and the Spanish Synagogue with its stunning Moorish interior. A combined ticket covers all six Jewish Museum sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhood for a local, less-touristy afternoon. Visit the quirky Žižkov Television Tower (with its famous crawling baby sculptures) for panoramic city views. Explore the vibrant local café culture and browse independent boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert or Mozart opera performance — Prague has world-class venues such as the Estates Theatre (where Mozart himself conducted Don Giovanni) or the Municipal House. Book tickets in advance online.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a local kavárna (café) — try Café Savoy for eggs, pastries, and quality coffee in a beautiful Art Nouveau setting
meals.lunch: Lunch in Josefov area — Café Nona or a nearby bistro; try goulash with bread or roasted pork knuckle
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Restaurace Mlejnice — hearty Czech food in a rustic cellar setting at very reasonable prices

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter requires a combined museum ticket (~350 CZK). Book concert or opera tickets several days in advance as performances sell out quickly in September.

day_by_day.morning: Morning free for personal exploration or optional day trip. Consider a half-day trip to Kutná Hora (~1 hour by train from Prague) to visit the famous Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) and the stunning Gothic Cathedral of Saint Barbara — a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague by early afternoon. Visit Wenceslas Square and the National Museum (Národní muzeum) — recently renovated, it offers rich exhibits on Czech history, natural history, and culture. Walk the length of the square and observe the vibrant city pulse.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Prague's craft beer scene in the evening. Visit a local pivnice (pub) such as Pivovarský Klub or Zly Casy, which offer dozens of Czech craft beers on tap. This is a great way to experience authentic local nightlife without splurging.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel or grab a trdelník (chimney cake) and coffee from a market stall before catching the train
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Restaurace Dačický — a historic restaurant serving traditional Bohemian dishes in a medieval setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local pub near Wenceslas Square — try fried cheese (smažený sýr) with tartar sauce, a beloved Czech pub staple, paired with a Kozel dark beer

day_by_day.notes: Kutná Hora trains depart from Prague Hlavní nádraží (main station) frequently. Round trip is affordable (~200 CZK). Book National Museum tickets online to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the scenic train or bus from Prague to Budapest (approximately 6–7 hours by train via RegioJet or FlixBus; book in advance for best mid-range fares). Enjoy the Central European countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest in the early-to-mid afternoon. Check into your Budapest accommodation, freshen up, and take an orientation walk along the Danube riverbank. Admire views of the Parliament Building from the Pest side — one of Europe's most spectacular riverside panoramas.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) if still open (closes ~18:00 on Saturdays), then head to the vibrant ruin bar district in the Jewish Quarter (VII district). Visit Szimpla Kert — Budapest's most famous ruin bar — for drinks and a unique cultural atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or pack snacks for the train journey
meals.lunch: Lunch on the train (RegioJet offers food service) or pack a picnic with Czech bread, cheese, and charcuterie from a Prague market
meals.dinner: First taste of Hungarian cuisine at Menza restaurant in Budapest — a retro-style bistro serving classic Hungarian dishes at mid-range prices; try gulyás (goulash) or pörkölt (meat stew)

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague–Budapest train tickets at least 2 weeks in advance via RegioJet.com for the best prices. Keep luggage manageable for easy transit. Validate Budapest transit tickets upon boarding public transport.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill — take the historic funicular (Budavári Sikló) up from the Chain Bridge. Visit Buda Castle and the Hungarian National Gallery inside. Walk to Fisherman's Bastion for fairy-tale turrets and breathtaking panoramic views over the Danube and Pest skyline. Visit the adjacent Matthias Church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Chain Bridge on foot back to Pest. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building — one of the world's most beautiful legislative buildings. Book a guided interior tour in advance (mandatory for non-EU visitors). Afterwards, stroll along Andrássy Avenue, a UNESCO-listed boulevard lined with grand neo-Renaissance mansions.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a traditional Hungarian thermal bath experience at Széchenyi Baths in City Park — the largest medicinal bath in Europe. The evening session (after 18:00) is less crowded and atmospheric under the lights.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Budapest café — try Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square for classic Hungarian pastries (rétes/strudel) and coffee in a grand setting
meals.lunch: Lunch near Castle Hill — Baltazár Budapest offers excellent burgers and Hungarian-inspired dishes in a relaxed garden setting at mid-range prices
meals.dinner: Dinner after the baths at a restaurant in City Park area or nearby Városliget — try Bagolyvár restaurant, known for traditional Hungarian home cooking at reasonable prices

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance at jegymester.hu. Bring a swimsuit and towel for Széchenyi Baths, or rent them on-site for a small fee. Sunday is a popular day — expect some crowds at major sights.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street — the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world. Explore the adjoining Hungarian Jewish Museum and the moving Holocaust Memorial Garden (Tree of Life sculpture). Then walk through the charming VII district (Erzsébetváros) Jewish Quarter neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the eclectic Inner City (Belváros) and the upscale Váci Street shopping area. Visit the Central Market Hall (same as Great Market Hall) for a deep dive into Hungarian food culture — pick up paprika, lángos (fried dough), túrós rétes (cottage cheese strudel), and Tokaji wine as souvenirs or snacks. Cross the Liberty Bridge for views and walk up Gellért Hill to the Citadella for a sweeping 360° panorama of Budapest.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a Danube river cruise at sunset — a magical way to see Budapest's illuminated bridges and landmarks from the water. Many mid-range cruise options include a welcome drink. Afterwards, explore the lively bar and restaurant scene on Gozsdu Udvar (Gozsdu Courtyard) in the Jewish Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local pékség (bakery) — try a fresh kifli (crescent roll) with butter and jam
meals.lunch: Lángos and strudel tasting at the Central Market Hall food stalls — affordable, authentic, and delicious
meals.dinner: Dinner at Costes Downtown or a mid-range Hungarian restaurant on Gozsdu Courtyard — try halászlé (fisherman's soup) or töltött káposzta (stuffed cabbage) with sour cream

day_by_day.notes: The Great Synagogue is closed on Saturdays (Shabbat). Monday is a good day to visit. Book the Danube river cruise in advance — sunset cruises are popular and fill up quickly. Gellért Hill climb takes about 20–30 minutes and is worth the effort.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Museum of Fine Arts or the Palace of Arts (MÜPA) in City Park. Stroll through the park and see Vajdahunyad Castle — a whimsical castle complex built for the 1896 Millennial Exhibition, combining Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque architectural styles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping on Váci Street or at the Central Market Hall. Pack up and prepare for departure. Enjoy a leisurely farewell coffee at one of Budapest's grand historic coffeehouses — New York Café (splurge-worthy for the stunning interior) or the more affordable Centrál Kávéház.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for departure. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before flight time for check-in, security, and boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast — try rántotta (scrambled eggs) with Hungarian sausage (kolbász) and fresh bread at a local étterem (restaurant)
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at Centrál Kávéház — classic Hungarian café food including soups, salads, and sandwiches in an elegant setting
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner near the hotel before heading to the airport

day_by_day.notes: Budapest airport is approximately 30–40 minutes from the city center by taxi or Airport Shuttle Minibus. Pre-book your airport transfer to avoid last-minute stress. Double-check flight departure time and terminal. Exchange any remaining Hungarian Forints (HUF) before leaving — it is not widely accepted outside Hungary.

day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Evening stroll through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) — Prague's most romantic quarter — lit beautifully at dusk. Enjoy an aperitif at a rooftop bar overlooking the castle.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate à la carte breakfast at the hotel restaurant — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and specialty Czech coffee
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Lokál Dlouhááá or Field Restaurant — modern Czech cuisine with seasonal ingredients; try svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) elevated to fine-dining standards
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering a tasting menu rooted in 19th-century Czech culinary heritage, paired with curated Czech and international wines

day_by_day.notes: Book La Degustation well in advance — tables are extremely limited. Wear comfortable walking shoes for cobblestone streets. September weather in Prague is typically mild (15–20°C), ideal for walking tours.

day_by_day.morning: Private cultural immersion: visit the hauntingly beautiful Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of the best-preserved Jewish historical districts in Europe. Tour the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Spanish Synagogue (stunning Moorish interior), and the Pinkas Synagogue (a Holocaust memorial). A private historian guide provides deeply moving and educational commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — Prague's bohemian, less-touristy districts. Visit the monumental Žižkov Television Tower (with its famous crawling baby sculptures) for panoramic city views. Browse independent boutiques, local galleries, and artisan coffee shops. Optional: private visit to the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a world-class classical music performance — Prague is renowned for its concert scene. Options include a chamber concert at the Estates Theatre (where Mozart himself conducted Don Giovanni in 1787) or the stunning Rudolfinum concert hall. Dress code: smart elegant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh Czech pastries (koláče), cold cuts, local honey, and a Viennese-style coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Savoy — a beautifully restored Neo-Renaissance café serving elevated Czech classics; try the cream of celeriac soup and Wiener schnitzel
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Alcron Restaurant (Radisson Blu Alcron Hotel) — Art Deco elegance, Michelin-recommended; seafood-forward tasting menu with exceptional wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter requires respectful attire (shoulders and knees covered). Book concert tickets well in advance through the venue's official website. September is peak cultural season in Prague — performances sell out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — optional sunrise walk across an empty Charles Bridge (magical before the crowds arrive). Return for a relaxed hotel breakfast. Optional wellness session at the hotel spa to recharge mid-trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer (approximately 4.5–5 hours by premium chauffeured car or opt for a scenic train in first class) from Prague to Budapest. Enjoy the rolling Central European countryside en route. Check in to your premium Budapest accommodation and settle in.
day_by_day.evening: First impressions of Budapest: take a private evening cruise on the Danube River. Witness the illuminated Parliament Building, Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, and Fisherman's Bastion — a UNESCO World Heritage panorama often called the most beautiful river view in Europe. Champagne served on board.

meals.breakfast: Final Prague breakfast at the hotel — indulgent spread with local jams, artisan breads, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic hamper prepared by the hotel for the journey — premium sandwiches, charcuterie, fruit, and sparkling water, or dine at a first-class restaurant car if traveling by train
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Budapest at Costes Restaurant — Budapest's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a sophisticated tasting menu blending Hungarian flavors with contemporary European technique; exceptional wine cellar featuring Tokaj wines

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private Danube cruise for the evening — sunset/twilight departure (around 19:30–20:00) offers the most spectacular lighting. Confirm transfer logistics at least 48 hours in advance. Private car is recommended for maximum comfort and flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Buda Castle District — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the Royal Palace (housing the Hungarian National Gallery), Matthias Church with its stunning geometric tile roof, and the fairytale-like Fisherman's Bastion with its seven towers representing the seven Magyar tribes. Breathtaking panoramic views over the Pest side and the Danube.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot to the Pest side. Visit the grand Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the largest parliament buildings in the world — on a private guided tour. Then explore Andrássy Avenue, Budapest's answer to the Champs-Élysées, a UNESCO-listed boulevard lined with Neo-Renaissance mansions, luxury boutiques, and grand cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House — one of the most beautiful opera houses in the world, rivaling Vienna's. Even if opera isn't your preference, the architecture alone is worth the visit. Alternatively, enjoy a private after-hours tour of the Opera House interior.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Hungarian specialties such as lángos (fried dough), túrós rétes (cheese strudel), and freshly brewed Hungarian coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Onyx Restaurant on Vörösmarty Square — two Michelin stars, elegant Hungarian haute cuisine; signature dishes include Hungarian foie gras and Mangalica pork preparations
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at the Grand Café of the New York Palace — one of the most ornate café-restaurants in the world, opened in 1894; indulge in Hungarian goulash, duck confit, and Tokaji Aszú dessert wine

day_by_day.notes: Book Opera House tickets and Onyx Restaurant well in advance — both are extremely popular. The New York Palace Grand Café is a must-experience Budapest institution regardless of its tourist popularity. Smart-casual to formal attire recommended for the opera.

day_by_day.morning: Immerse yourself in Budapest's legendary thermal bath culture — a 2,000-year-old tradition dating to Roman times. Visit the magnificent Széchenyi Thermal Bath (the largest in Europe) or the ornate Gellért Thermal Bath for a private VIP cabin experience. Enjoy mineral-rich thermal pools, steam rooms, and optional massage treatments. A quintessential Budapest luxury experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's largest and most spectacular indoor market, housed in a stunning 1897 iron-and-tile building. Browse stalls of Hungarian paprika, Tokaj wines, artisan salami, hand-painted folk ceramics, and embroidered textiles. Purchase premium local gifts and souvenirs. Then visit the Jewish Quarter (VII District) — home to the Great Synagogue (the largest in Europe) and the ruin bar district (romkocsmák), a uniquely Budapest phenomenon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar — 360 Bar atop the Párisi Udvar or High Note SkyBar at the Aria Hotel offer spectacular 360-degree views over Budapest's skyline. Then a leisurely evening stroll along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó).

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before heading to the thermal baths — yogurt, granola, fresh fruit, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Borkonyha WineKitchen — a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant specializing in Hungarian wines paired with creative modern dishes; excellent selection of indigenous grape varieties like Furmint and Kadarka
meals.dinner: Dinner at Stand Restaurant — one of Budapest's most celebrated fine-dining establishments, helmed by chef Széll Tamás (MasterChef Hungary winner); modern Hungarian cuisine at its absolute finest with an outstanding wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book a private VIP cabin at the thermal baths for maximum luxury and privacy — avoid the public pools on weekends if possible as they can be crowded. The Great Synagogue requires modest dress and is closed on Saturdays (Shabbat) — visit Sunday is ideal. Reserve Stand Restaurant at least 2–3 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Danube Bend (Dunakanyar) — one of Central Europe's most scenic landscapes, just 40 km north of Budapest. Private chauffeured car takes you to the medieval hilltop citadel of Visegrád (spectacular Danube views), then to the charming baroque town of Szentendre — a living open-air museum of Serbian Orthodox churches, cobblestone lanes, artist studios, and artisan galleries. Visit the Hungarian Open Air Museum (Skanzen) for insight into traditional rural Hungarian life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Esztergom — Hungary's most sacred city and former royal capital. Visit the magnificent Esztergom Basilica, the largest church in Hungary, perched dramatically above the Danube with views into Slovakia across the river. Explore the Castle Museum and the Bakócz Chapel — a Renaissance masterpiece. Private guide provides rich historical narrative throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Budapest by late afternoon. Relax at the hotel. Final evening: private farewell dinner experience — a traditional Hungarian folk music and dance performance combined with a premium dinner at a historic Budapest venue.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast before departure — Hungarian cold cuts, pickled vegetables, fresh breads, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch in Szentendre at Rab Ráby Restaurant — a charming historic restaurant serving authentic Hungarian cuisine in a 18th-century setting; try halászlé (fisherman's soup) and stuffed cabbage
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Kistücsök or Alabárdos Restaurant in the Buda Castle District — intimate, candlelit atmosphere with live Hungarian folk music; traditional dishes like chicken paprikash, beef pörkölt, and chimney cake (kürtőskalács) for dessert, paired with premium Tokaj wines

day_by_day.notes: The Danube Bend excursion covers approximately 120–150 km round trip — a private car is essential. Start early (by 9:00) to maximize time at all three stops. September light is beautiful for photography at Visegrád and Esztergom. Confirm folk music dinner reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last-minute exploration of a neighborhood you haven't fully discovered: consider the elegant Lipótváros (Leopold Town) district around St. Stephen's Basilica, or browse the luxury boutiques along Váci Street. Visit St. Stephen's Basilica and ascend to the dome for a final panoramic view over the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: optional visit to the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) — one of Central Europe's finest art collections housed in a stunning Neo-Classical building, featuring works by Raphael, El Greco, Goya, and Rembrandt. Or indulge in a final spa treatment at the hotel. Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry with you memories of two of Europe's most magnificent capitals — Prague's Gothic mystery and Budapest's grand imperial splendor — along with premium wines, thermal waters, and world-class cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final hotel breakfast — the full spread, savored slowly; order the Hungarian breakfast platter with mangalica sausage, fresh peppers, tomatoes, and cottage cheese
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most iconic café since 1858; enjoy dobos torte (the legendary Hungarian layered cake), Eszterházy cake, and a grand café coffee in opulent Belle Époque surroundings
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dining at Budapest Liszt Ferenc Airport (Sky Court Lounge)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport procedures. Arrange private transfer to the airport in advance — traffic can be unpredictable during Monday afternoon rush. Consider purchasing premium Hungarian souvenirs: Tokaji Aszú wine (5 or 6 puttonyos), Herend porcelain, Unicum liqueur, and premium Hungarian paprika as gifts.
